This is terrible advice for most investors. For Newfound Gold's primary project, it appears that the gold is not located in a defined area that can be mined profitably and efficiently (this is why a group of investors in Canada shorted NFG a few years ago for a profit). Check out the history and you will see that they have been drilling and drilling for years without a plan for production at its primary project site. It appears that Newfound Gold purchased a small project that may be producing a small amount of gold so they can now say they are in production - which is misleading.  I also agree with other posts which explain that these billionaires can get in at pennies per share and then make 5X+ when average retail investors push the price up while the project is still in its exploration or permitting phase. The billionaires then sell their initial investment and the shares they hold onto, if any, are basically free. Also, many of the projects recommended in this video are located in Mexico and other foreign countries which are no longer considered safe for the average retail investor. Many of these billionaires invest in hundreds of these early exploration companies and hope that a few of them pay off and offset the losers which are the majority of these early exploration companies. Question: Are the billionaires paying for videos like this to draw small investors into these challenged projects?
